description: Elissaios Sarmas and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The documented building-automation service monitors multiple facility subsystems and disaggregates consumption across floors and rooms. Its application to a real multistorey building provides benchmarking indicators and information for the energy manager. The abstract identifies heating, cooling, ventilation, hot water and lighting as relevant systems, without stating that all are separately metered in the case. The site name, study period and quantitative savings are unspecified. This case supports assessment of an actual building-monitoring and control service, while the broader MATRYCS analytics platform is represented separately. No complete raw measurement release is inferred. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
